name: frostbite-switch
title: Frostbite Switch
description: iOS-style switch whose OFF state grows dendritic ice across the track; switching ON melts it in reverse with droplet run-off before the thumb springs over.
instruction: Build an iOS-style toggle (real <button role=switch aria-checked>, 52x30 track, 26px thumb, rounded-full) with a canvas 2D overlay clipped to the track (DPR clamp 2). On switch-to-OFF, 5-7 seeded stochastic branching walkers grow a dendritic ice skin from the thumb's leading edge: 2px steps at 140 px/s, heading jitter +/-25 deg, child-branch probability 0.15/step, max depth 4, stroke width tapering 1.4 to 0.6px by depth, ~700ms total, mulberry32-seeded per state-change so regrowth is deterministic in-session. On switch-to-ON, melt traverses segments in reverse growth order over 450ms while 6-10 droplets detach (gravity 1200 px/s^2, 400ms lifetime, fade out); the thumb slide starts 120ms into the melt on a spring (k=170 s^-2, zeta=0.85, one small overshoot) and the track ramps an accent-tinted glow over 200ms. Idle OFF state breathes crystal-layer opacity +/-0.06 at 0.2 Hz by mutating canvas style opacity only (no redraw), paused offscreen via IntersectionObserver and when the document is hidden; rAF fully sleeps at grow/melt end states. Crystal ink ramps --foreground (trunks) toward --border (tips) with tapering alpha, all colors read via getComputedStyle at mount and re-derived on a MutationObserver watching documentElement class changes so ice is visible on both themes. Accent focus-visible ring, token-relative hover border, disabled renders crystals at 40% opacity with no shimmer, prefers-reduced-motion swaps to two static frames (full crystal OFF / clear ON) with a snapping thumb. Guard zero-size tracks before seeding walkers; tear down every observer, listener, and rAF on unmount and free the segment arrays.
